g\u00e9n\u00e9rative efficace en m\u00e9moire pour l'apprentissage incr\u00e9mental par classes dans la reconnaissance des activit\u00e9s humaines<\/jats:title>\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\"fr\">L'utilisation croissante d'appareils intelligents, tels que les smartphones et les smartwatches, a augment\u00e9 la disponibilit\u00e9 des donn\u00e9es collect\u00e9es aupr\u00e8s des utilisateurs dans leurs activit\u00e9s quotidiennes.  Ces donn\u00e9es, recueillies par des capteurs int\u00e9gr\u00e9s, permettent de former des mod\u00e8les d'apprentissage automatique pour la reconnaissance de l'activit\u00e9 humaine (HAR) et le d\u00e9veloppement de syst\u00e8mes intelligents pour la surveillance de la sant\u00e9 et le diagnostic, ainsi que des services personnalis\u00e9s. Malgr\u00e9 ces progr\u00e8s, les mod\u00e8les d'apprentissage automatique form\u00e9s sur des flux de donn\u00e9es continus sont confront\u00e9s \u00e0 un probl\u00e8me majeur: l'oubli catastrophique. Ce probl\u00e8me survient lorsque les mod\u00e8les ne parviennent pas \u00e0 conserver les activit\u00e9s pr\u00e9c\u00e9demment apprises tout en essayant de s'adapter aux nouvelles activit\u00e9s introduites par les utilisateurs. Pour rem\u00e9dier \u00e0 ce probl\u00e8me, l'apprentissage continu (CL) est apparu comme une solution permettant aux mod\u00e8les d'apprendre \u00e0 partir de flux de donn\u00e9es \u00e9volutifs tout en minimisant l'oubli des connaissances ant\u00e9rieures. Parmi les approches propos\u00e9es, celles bas\u00e9es sur la relecture sont reconnues comme prometteuses pour maintenir la pr\u00e9cision des anciennes connaissances. Cependant, leur succ\u00e8s repose sur l'\u00e9quilibre entre les contraintes de m\u00e9moire et la qualit\u00e9 des \u00e9chantillons s\u00e9lectionn\u00e9s pour la relecture. Cette th\u00e8se aborde cette question en proposant deux approches de relecture g\u00e9n\u00e9rative et un protocole exp\u00e9rimental dans le cadre de l'apprentissage incr\u00e9mental par classe dans HAR. Tout d'abord, nous pr\u00e9sentons TaskVAE, une approche peu gourmande en m\u00e9moire qui entra\u00eene un autoencodeur variationnel (VAE) l\u00e9ger et sp\u00e9cifique \u00e0 la t\u00e2che afin de g\u00e9n\u00e9rer des donn\u00e9es synth\u00e9tiques pour les activit\u00e9s pass\u00e9es. Il a \u00e9t\u00e9 d\u00e9montr\u00e9 que la TaskVAE am\u00e9liore de mani\u00e8re significative la pr\u00e9cision du classificateur par rapport \u00e0 la relecture bas\u00e9e sur des exemples, avec un budget m\u00e9moire \u00e9quivalent. Identifiant la qualit\u00e9 des \u00e9chantillons g\u00e9n\u00e9r\u00e9s comme un facteur cl\u00e9, nous avons ensuite d\u00e9velopp\u00e9 TaskVAE-GMM, une m\u00e9thode am\u00e9lior\u00e9e qui int\u00e8gre des mod\u00e8les de m\u00e9lange gaussien (GMM) pour structurer l'espace latent de la VAE pendant le processus de g\u00e9n\u00e9ration d'\u00e9chantillons. En \u00e9chantillonnant \u00e0 partir de grappes bas\u00e9es sur la densit\u00e9, TaskVAE-GMM produit des donn\u00e9es synth\u00e9tiques de meilleure qualit\u00e9, permettant une r\u00e9tention plus efficace des connaissances des t\u00e2ches pr\u00e9c\u00e9demment apprises. Gr\u00e2ce \u00e0 des exp\u00e9riences approfondies utilisant le protocole d'\u00e9valuation propos\u00e9, TaskVAE-GMM surpasse les m\u00e9thodes de relecture g\u00e9n\u00e9rative et de relecture d'exp\u00e9rience existantes dans tous les domaines, ce qui en fait une solution robuste et efficace pour la construction de syst\u00e8mes de HAR adaptatifs et \u00e9volutifs capables d'apprendre de mani\u00e8re incr\u00e9mentielle dans des environnements r\u00e9els.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.70675\/eb3fa5b2za166z4620z9d34z7bc2a9d06656","type":"dissertation","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Memory-Efficient Generative Replay for Class-Incremental Learning in Human Activity Recognition"],"author":[{"given":"Bonpagna","family":"Kann","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"id":[{"id":"https:\/\/ror.org\/02rx3b187","id-type":"ROR","asserted-by":"publisher"}],"name":"Universit\u00e9 Grenoble Alpes"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.70675\/eb3fa5b2za166z4620z9d34z7bc2a9d06656"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Replay-free class-incremental vibration diagnosis must incorporate new fault categories after deployment while retaining earlier decisions without storing old signals. Sequential optimization is difficult in this setting because it can distort both individual class representatives and their relative geometry, especially when vibration patterns also vary with operating conditions. We introduce graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), which represents each observed class by a prototype and connects related prototypes through a sparse feature-space graph. New-class samples initialize new nodes and local edges, whereas node- and edge-stability terms constrain changes to the previously learned class structure. The graph is learned from embeddings rather than predefined fault taxonomies, and its retained state scales with the number of classes instead of the number of vibration windows. A leakage-resistant evaluation protocol is specified for four public bearing datasets and jointly measures cumulative-class accuracy, old-class forgetting, new-class learning, and robustness to operating-condition shifts. This paper addresses the resulting replay-free class-incremental vibration fault diagnosis problem. We propose graph continual prototype learning (GCPL), a compact AI-based diagnostic framework that stores class prototypes, diagonal dispersion estimates, and a sparse relation graph instead of previous signal windows. New classes are inserted locally, while prototype anchoring, old-edge consistency, neighborhood-rank preservation, reliability weighting, and a topology-aware boundary margin constrain destabilization of the retained class structure. Record- or bearing-level splits are applied before windowing on CWRU, Paderborn, XJTU-SY, and JNU to avoid overlapping-window leakage. Across four datasets and five matched seeds, GCPL attains AIA values of 95.1%, 91.2%, 89.5%, and 92.4%, improving on the strongest replay-free baseline by 2.1\u20132.6 points and reducing final-session forgetting by 1.8\u20132.3 points. Additional tests cover relation drift, operating-condition shift, additive noise, low-shot and long-tail increments, class order, calibration, and retained-state efficiency. The results indicate that preserving inter-class topology is an effective compact memory mechanism for adaptive vibration faces two critical limitations: Each client&apos;s replay buffer stores its own historical samples, preventing crucial knowledge from being transferred across clients. Privacy information can be uncovered by millions or billions of parameters, and the upload of parameter updates to server is extremely high-exhausting. To overcome these challenges, we propose \\textbf{FedCACH}: a novel method that \\textbf{Fed}eratively \\textbf{CACH}es regularized pseudo-word embeddings uploaded to the server to facilitate cross-client knowledge transfer with manageable communication and computation\u00a0 costs. Specifically, FedCACH leverages diffusion models for bidirectional text-image conversion. Clients perform regularized image-to-text prompt learning to generate regularized pseudo-word embeddings. They represent client knowledge with respect to client privacy. The server aggregates and caches these regularized pseudo-word embeddings into a buffer, using them as knowledgeable guidance cues for text-to-image synthesis. The resulting synthetic images, embodying aggregated cross-client knowledge, are used to replay in server-side incremental tasks. The replayed global model is then redistributed to clients for personalized finetuning. Experiments demonstrate the feasibility and privacy of client-side prompt learning under moderate computation budgets.
